assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology led to incretin-based drugs that transformed treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity, with cardiovascular and renal benefit; an unusually clear chain from gene-product discovery to physiological mechanism to broad clinical change in the field.
assessment.attribution: Drucker and Holst established GLP-1 biology and its therapeutic action, and Mojsov's identification of the active peptide form is a decisive early contribution; Knudsen's medicinal-chemistry/industrial role is important but would exceed a three-person prize. Priority among other early contributors (e.g. Habener, not on the credited list) is unresolved.
assessment.maturity: Large randomized outcome trials and real-world use give strong independent confirmation, and the clinical impact is now very visible, so recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Fair allocation of credit between basic discovery, peptide chemistry and drug development is contested.
Long-term safety and durability of effects are still being defined.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The unfolded protein response revealed a new mode of organelle-to-nucleus signalling (IRE1, HAC1/XBP1, ATF6), a conceptual advance in cell biology with lasting influence on proteostasis, secretory physiology and disease.
assessment.attribution: Walter and Mori independently and complementarily defined the pathway, giving a clean two-person configuration; I am not aware of a competing primary claim, though I have not verified this.
assessment.maturity: Mechanism has been confirmed across yeast and mammals for 25+ years, with stable interpretation and extensive follow-up.
uncertainties: Direct medical translation is still limited compared with clinical candidates.
Role in specific human diseases remains partly correlative.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Engineered CAR-T cells produced durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies and created a new class of living therapeutics; the impact on cancer treatment is major and recognized.
assessment.attribution: June (clinical CD19 CAR-T translation) and Sadelain (CD28 costimulation and CAR design) were decisive; Eshhar's early chimeric receptor and Rosenberg's adoptive-transfer work complicate a fair configuration, and I would not rely on names outside the supplied credited list.
assessment.maturity: Multiple approved products and long follow-up confirm efficacy in hematologic cancer; solid-tumour benefit is unproven and toxicity and access remain issues.
uncertainties: Credit sharing with early chimeric-receptor pioneers is difficult.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Demonstrating that the thymus and the bursa/bone marrow generate distinct T- and B-lymphocyte lineages established the foundation of adaptive immunity and later clinical immunology.
assessment.attribution: Miller identified thymic function in T-cell development; Cooper (with Good and Peterson's bursa work) defined B-cell lineage; a two-person prize is defensible, though others contributed to the early work, which I cannot verify in detail.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature and universally accepted; the main issue is that the laureates are elderly, so recognition is overdue rather than premature.
uncertainties: Contributions of other early investigators may complicate attribution.
Age of the principals makes timing urgent.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Virus-like-particle HPV vaccines prevent persistent infection and cervical and other HPV-related cancers, with large public-health effect and evidence of population-level reductions in disease.
assessment.attribution: Lowy and Schiller developed the L1 VLP concept and Frazer (with Zhou) the related expression and vaccine route; a three-person configuration is plausible but the Frazer/Zhou credit and parallel industrial work remain contested.
assessment.maturity: Strong trial evidence and national registry data show reductions in cervical precancer and cancer; the discovery is mature and timely, although it follows the 2008 prize for HPV as a cause of cancer.
uncertainties: Late-career recognition of J. Zhou is a credit issue not resolvable from the supplied names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: TOR/mTOR defines a central regulator of cell growth and metabolism with broad relevance to cancer, ageing, immunology and metabolism; a major conceptual discovery.
assessment.attribution: Hall discovered TOR in yeast and its role in growth control; Sabatini identified mammalian mTOR and the nutrient-sensing complexes; Schreiber's rapamycin-target work and others (Heitman) complicate the configuration.
assessment.maturity: Extensively confirmed, with therapeutic application in transplantation and oncology, though disease-specific benefit is more modest than the biology suggests.
uncertainties: Dispute over credit among TOR and mTOR discoverers.
Clinical translation lags behind the basic impact.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: BCL-2 and its family established that cell survival, not just proliferation, drives cancer, and led to BH3 mimetics such as venetoclax; a conceptual and translational advance.
assessment.attribution: Cory and Adams are the central researchers on BCL-2 function in lymphoma; Vaux and Strasser contributed important functional work but a prize is limited to three; Tsujimoto and Korsmeyer are not on the credited list and would be relevant to priority.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with approved drugs and strong independent confirmation; apoptosis was already honoured in 2002 so the novelty case is narrower.
uncertainties: Priority involving people absent from the credited names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Showing that TNF is a dominant driver in rheumatoid arthritis and that its blockade is effective changed the treatment of inflammatory disease worldwide.
assessment.attribution: Feldmann and Maini made the decisive mechanistic and clinical proof of concept; a two-person prize is clean, but antibody engineers and anti-TNF developers are not credited here.
assessment.maturity: Decades of clinical use and extensive trial confirmation make this mature and well established.
uncertainties: Biologic development was shared with several other groups.
Newer therapies reduce the sense of recency.
